guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the equipment age that makes a replacement lead, the renewal rate you want, the technicians who run tune-ups and the cost of a reminder.
Check Agreement Plans, Technicians and Equipment Types. They hold your plans, your lead technicians and the replacement ticket of each equipment type.

List every customer on Customer Sites by site reference, area and phone, and every piece of equipment on Equipment with type, install date, make, model and serial. Age and the lead score fill in by themselves.
Enter each maintenance agreement on Agreements and each renewal that came due on Renewals. Days left, the renewal flag and the ranking of renewals due fill in by themselves.
Plan each tune-up on Tune-up Visits with its window, planned date, date done and status. Behind, overdue and the value of the visit calculate themselves.
Write each reminder you send on Campaign List with its channel and whether it booked a tune-up or sold an agreement. Campaign Results counts them by month.
Type the month starts on Agreement Book by Month, Visits Due by Month and Campaign Results. The counts, the recurring revenue and the rates calculate themselves.
Type the profit inputs on Agreement Profit and Member Revenue from your own jobs, and the share you expect to replace on Equipment by Age Band.
Use the 18 tools: each answers one question with a verdict. Change the yellow inputs to try another plan, price, channel or number of technicians.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.

Read the Sites, Equipment and Agreements Dashboard and the Charts every week. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets as the customer book; a shop with a dispatcher uses the dispatcher columns.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Contractor Excel Template: Customer Sites, Equipment, Maintenance Agreements, Tune-up Schedule, Renewals
listing.headline: Your customer book: sites, equipment, maintenance agreements and tune-ups
listing.description:
Run the customer side of an HVAC and plumbing contractor business in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-run residential and light-commercial service shop with 1 to 15 technicians, an office manager who also dispatches, and a van for each lead technician. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets as a customer book; a shop with a dispatcher uses the dispatcher columns.

Customer Sites holds every site by reference, area, site type and phone, with no personal names. Equipment keeps type, fuel, install date, make, model, serial and last service, and works out the age, a lead score and a call now, mail or hold verdict. Agreements, Renewals and Tune-up Visits hold the maintenance agreement book: plan, price, renewal date, status, the two seasonal windows and what is behind. The Agreement Book by Month shows new, renewed, ended and running agreements with monthly recurring revenue and your renewal rate.

18 tools answer weekly questions with a clear verdict: an aged equipment lead list, renewals ranked by value, the open tune-up window against last year, tune-up months against technician hours, agreement profit by plan, a pre-season campaign planner with cost per booked tune-up, a lapse analyser and a 12-month recurring revenue forecast. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents such as the agreement summary and the renewal notice, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to customers, landlord accounts, technicians, your office, your equipment supplier and the accountant.

This is part six of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no per-technician fee: you keep your data. A demo copy full of sample data and a blank copy are included. It helps you keep track of your business and does not promise results.
